newsitem.title: INDIA: India budget to revive capital markets, growth - CII.
newsitem.headline: India budget to revive capital markets, growth - CII.

text.p: The Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) said on Friday the 1997/98 (April-March) budget would kick-start depressed capital markets and spur industrial growth.

Corporate tax cuts, the removal of a surcharge on profits tax, and the abolition of dividend income taxation were "strong, positive signals" that would boost investment and production, CII said in a statement.
"CII believes the budget will see the Sensex (Bombay stock exchange sensitive index) zooming," it said, citing new rules on buying back shares and intercorporate loans.
Blue chips staged a sizzling rally at Bombay bourses in reaction to the budget. The benchmark Bombay index jumped 178.20 points or 5.13 percent to 3,652.99 in a special post-budget trading session.
The industry body said it supported Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's tax proposals, which restructured personal taxation and broadened the tax base.
"The focus and priority given to infrastructure in the 1997 budget was critical," it said.
But customs duty on capital goods and excise duty on certain critical inputs remained high, the statement quoted CII president Shekhar Datta as saying.
It said Chidambaram's proposal to allow state firms' joint ventures in health insurance was a welcome step that paved the way for opening the insurance sector.
